desk.headline: Revenue up 7% to $387.7m, adjusted EPS $1.83 beats; no formal guidance, AccentCare deal set for Q1 2027
results: Revenue rose 7% to $387.7m, led by personal care (78% of sales), which grew 9% with help from the HomeCourt purchase and earlier state rate rises.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 13.5% to $51.2m and adjusted EPS rose 17% to $1.83; GAAP EPS was $1.54 against $1.24.
Hospice revenue was flat at $69.0m but up 8.8% organically once a one-off benefit last year is stripped out; home health returned to organic growth.
Cash stood at $98.5m against bank debt of $24.3m, with $617.8m available on the revolving credit line.
Addus agreed to buy AccentCare's personal care division (outside New York) for about $275m, adding roughly $280m of yearly revenue.

guidance.summary: Addus does not publish formal guidance. On the call, management pointed to a full-year adjusted EBITDA margin of around 13%, a seasonal Q4 gross margin lift and state rate support of 3–5% in early 2027.

points: The AccentCare deal has cleared the federal antitrust wait and should close in Q1 2027, paid from cash and the revolver; management expects it to add to earnings.
AccentCare's lower margins will pull the 2027 EBITDA margin a little below this year's roughly 13% until cost savings come through.
Personal care client numbers dipped slightly in low-hour cases as caregivers want full 40-hour weeks; Q4 census is seen flat to slightly up.
New Mexico granted about a 4% rate rise from July; Texas and Illinois rate decisions come when their legislatures meet in 2027.
Management does not expect Medicaid work requirements to hurt revenue, as most clients should be exempt.
